What must be reported: Whether host reads were removed before viral screening; host-removal tool and host reference version
Consequence if omitted: Fractions are not comparable across studies
Effect measured in this study: ≤1.2% (C2 vs C6); larger when host content is high

What must be reported: Database name and version (e.g., RVDB-prot v32 Unique, nr, study-assembled vOTUs); whether a study-specific catalogue was used
Which functional categories of viral-like hits were retained; whether hits to host-homologous categories were excluded, and on what rule
Consequence if omitted: Host-homologous hits are counted as viral

What must be reported: Read counts, contig counts, or abundance-weighted values; abundance threshold applied
Consequence if omitted: Estimates are over- or underestimated and non-comparable

What must be reported: Whether dual negative controls were run (shuffled sequences; reversed database) and the number of hits obtained
Consequence if omitted: A 0.1% estimate cannot be distinguished from zero

What must be reported: Assembler and version; N50; whether sequencing depth was considered when calling shared or unique vOTUs
Consequence if omitted: Shared and unique calls are unreliable

What must be reported: Tool and version; confidence threshold; whether predictions were externally validated; taxonomic rank reported
Number of independent assays and the criterion applied in each
Consequence if omitted: A reported zero is not credible
